title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs', an abstract, combinatorial setting for tame/polyhedral geometry. M is a set of 'figures' carrying the following structure:
- a containment order X' ≪ X;
- a face/stratum order P ≤ Q;
- a disjointness relation X ∥ Y ('disposition');
- a trace (restriction) operation X ↦ X_P, with X_P ≪ X and X_P ≪ P;
- an empty figure ∅.
The 'lieux' are the minimal nonempty elements of M for ≪, i.e. atoms. omb(X) (the 'ombre', or shadow, of X) is the set of atoms x ≪ X.

On the previous page Grothendieck stated:
- Ax L2: X ∥ Y iff every atom of X is disjoint from every atom of Y.
- Ax L3: atoms in the open shadows of distinct strata are disjoint.
He then proposed Ax CL(spéc), a compatibility criterion for 'neighbouring' figures X, Y with L = X ∧ Y. It says that X and Y are compatible as soon as every atom of X outside omb(L) is disjoint from every atom of Y outside omb(L).

This page proves that, under L2, CL(spéc) implies the original compatibility axiom C(spéc). The condition of C(spéc) is:
(A) for all X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y with X'_L = Y'_L = ∅, one has X' ∥ Y'.
The proof runs as follows.
1. By L2 it suffices to show x ∥ y for atoms x ∈ omb(X') ⊂ omb(X) and y ∈ omb(Y') ⊂ omb(Y).
2. Since x ≪ X', we get x_L ≪ X'_L = ∅, so x_L = ∅.
3. By Lemma 1 (which uses L ≤ X), x_L = ∅ means x ∉ omb(L). The same holds for y.
4. So x ∈ omb(X)∖omb(L) and y ∈ omb(Y)∖omb(L), and the hypothesis (AL) gives x ∥ y.
Hence (AL) implies (A). He remarks that the premises used are L ≤ X and L ≤ Y.

Lemma 1: for P ≤ Q and an atom x ∈ omb(Q), x_P = ∅ iff x ∉ omb(P). Proof: x_P ≪ x and x is minimal nonzero. So x_P ≠ ∅ iff x_P = x, iff x ≪ P (one direction because x_P ≪ P; the other because x ≪ P forces x_P = x).

Lemma 2: for P ≤ Q and F ≪ Q, F_P = ∅ iff F ∥ P. One implication uses Ax D; the other follows from axioms 1–7 alone.

The following page tabulates the logical relations among the axioms C, D, D0, L1, L2, L3, CL(spac/pol).
errors: In (A) the conclusion is written 'X ∥ Y' but must be X' ∥ Y'. Likewise 'X' ∈ omb(X)' should read X' ≪ X: X' ranges over subfigures, not atoms.
Lemma 1's step 'x_P = x implies x ≪ P' tacitly uses x_P ≪ P (a property of the trace operation); this is not stated on the page.
Only the sufficiency direction (AL) ⇒ (A) is proved. The margin of the previous page notes that necessity ('il faut et il suffit') is wanted but not obtained.

ideas.what: Reducing disjointness and compatibility of figures to disjointness of their atoms ('lieux') via the shadow omb(X)
ideas.modern_name: Atomistic lattice / point-set reduction in an axiomatic tame (o-minimal/polyhedral) geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lattice-theoretic atomism (Birkhoff); tame topology axiomatics (van den Dries, o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced only programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Lemma 1: an atom has empty trace on P iff it is not contained in P
Lemma 2: for P ≤ Q and F ≪ Q, F_P = ∅ iff F ∥ P (one direction needs Ax D)

missed.claim: Whether the atom-wise compatibility criterion CL(spéc) is also necessary (an equivalence) is left open. Here only sufficiency is proved. The next page develops the logical bookkeeping between the axioms C, D, D0, L1–L3 and CL.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor point in an unpublished axiomatization of tame topology. It is of interest mainly to anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's 'analysis situs' program, not as an open problem in its own right.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of routine lemmas inside Grothendieck's private axiomatics for tame topology. It is historically interesting as part of the unpublished 'analysis situs', but the mathematics is elementary atom/trace bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'Comb(...)' throughout should read 'omb(...)' (ombre/shadow), as on the previous page.
'A1 CL', 'A1 D', 'A1 1 – A1 7' should read 'Ax CL', 'Ax D', 'Ax 1 – Ax 7'.
'Le lemme dit [?]' is likely 'Le lemme dit' (referring to L2) and introduces x ∈ omb(X') ⊂ omb(X).
The first line of the Lemma 2 discussion reads '(moyennant Ax D)'. The phrase 'pour P ≤ P' likely reads 'P ≤ Q, F ≪ Q'.
